normalization: Removed whole-response JSON Markdown fence; no field edits.

response.record_grain: One record per OCDS release in the top-level releases array (one publication event), with the first contract, first award and the supplier/procuringEntity parties bound by role.
response.grain_rationale: The inspector's record_path is releases, so each row is a release/publication event. Nested contracts, awards, items and parties are not exploded; the mapping reads the first contract (contracts[0]) and the role-bound supplier_party and procuring_entity_party bindings, which refuse multiple matches rather than silently selecting one.

record_id.rationale: releases[].id identifies exactly one published release, which is the row grain, so it is the traceable record key. ocid identifies the contracting process, not the release.

fields.rationale: The supplier party's single published name is the only name the source states for the supplier. The publisher does not distinguish registered from trading names, so it is recorded as stated and no legal form is inferred from forms such as 'The Trustee for ... Trust' or 'Data#3 Limited'.

The supplier party's additional identifier is an ABN only when the scheme is AU-ABN; the checksum transform validates it rather than length-checking. An ABN is an identifier only and proves nothing about legal form.
The locality of the supplier party's own stated address is exactly what address.locality holds for a business.

The supplier address region is an Australian state/territory abbreviation (NT, QLD, VIC, ACT) matching the address.state enum. ext.entity.operating_region is not used because a stated address region is not a claimed service footprint.
The postal code of the supplier party's stated address, re-padded for 3-digit NT codes.
The country of the supplier party's stated address as written (AUSTRALIA, COLOMBIA, SWITZERLAND, UNITED ARAB EMIRATES), which is what address.country stores.
The supplier contact point publishes role mailboxes (procurement@niaa.gov.au); the concept already stores role mailboxes and drops personal ones.
Australian numbers normalised to E.164; the concept already encodes the area-code rule and the mobile-as-personal-data caution.
The procuring entity party's single published name is the only name the source states for it. The procurement role does not by itself establish legal form, ownership or company-wide scope.
The procuring entity party's additional identifier is an ABN only when the scheme is AU-ABN; the checksum transform validates it. An ABN is an identifier only and proves nothing about legal form.
The locality of the procuring entity's own stated address, which is what address.locality holds for a business.
The procuring entity address region is an Australian state/territory abbreviation matching the address.state enum.
The postal code of the procuring entity's stated address, re-padded for 3-digit NT codes.
The procuring entity contact point publishes role mailboxes (tenders@finance.gov.au); the concept already stores role mailboxes and drops personal ones.
The publisher's contract notice identifier (e.g. CN4280221) identifies the notice across snapshots and links amendments; it is not a supplier key, ABN or ACN.

The date the contract was signed as stated in the notice; the published time component is a publication artefact and is dropped. It is not the contract start date, the notice publication date, or the business's registration date.
The first day of the contract period stated in the notice; it is the start of this contract's term, not the release publication date and not the moment the notice was observed.
The last day of the contract period stated in the notice, i.e. the planned end of this contract's term. It is not a licence expiry and not a business's cessation.
The scope of work as the procuring entity described it in the notice. It is source-stated activity text and describes this procurement, not the supplier's company-wide industry or sector.
The total maximum value of the contract over its life as reported in the notice, qualified by the published ISO 4217 currency. It is not annual expenditure, not revenue or business income.
The ISO 4217 alphabetic currency code published with the contract value, so the currency qualifier on dyn.contract.value is always explicit and the amount is never read unqualified.

The contract status as reported in the notice at extraction time, expressed with the OCDS contract status codelist and 'unknown' for anything not published. It is not the supplier's registration status.

The classification code of a contracted item as published, always paired with the publisher's scheme (here UNSPSC). The code describes the goods or services bought under this contract, not the supplier's company-wide industry.

How the contract was let as reported in the notice, expressed with the OCDS procurement method codelist and 'unknown' if not published. It describes the procurement process only and says nothing about contract size, supplier capability or the notice population.

Whether the notice marks the limited tender as exempt, published as 1 or 0 and mapped to true/false; a blank value is 'unknown', never false. It records a stated procurement exemption, not a judgement about whether the exemption was justified.

The exemption clause code the publisher gives for a limited tender (e.g. TR, AD), kept as stated. The code refers to a Commonwealth procurement exemption clause, which the verbatim reason text quotes.

The publisher's full wording of the reason a limited tender was used, kept verbatim as source evidence with its clause numbering and headings. It is a reported justification, not an assessment made by us.

supplier.rationale: The party bound by roles containing 'supplier' is the awarded supplier business. Its publisher party id is the record-local key; the ABN is the published identifier where available. A supplier name is not a unique entity key.

procuring_entity.rationale: The party bound by roles containing 'procuringEntity' is the government buyer business. The procurement role does not by itself establish legal form, ownership or company-wide scope.

contract.rationale: The first contract in the release is the contract notice entity, keyed by the publisher's notice number (contracts[0].id). It is not a business, licence or facility, and its value is not annual expenditure.

relationships.rationale: The contract notice names the supplier party as an awarded supplier (awards[0].suppliers[0].id matching parties[].id where roles includes supplier). An award may name several suppliers and each must be linked separately, never collapsed into one.

The contract notice names the procuring entity party as the buyer (parties[].id where roles includes procuringEntity). The role is a procurement role in this process and does not by itself establish legal form, ownership or company-wide scope.

unmapped.reason: roles is the discriminator used to bind supplier_party and procuring_entity_party; its meaning is already carried by the CONTRACT_AWARDED_TO and CONTRACT_PROCURED_BY relationships, so a separate role claim would duplicate them.
roles is the discriminator used to bind the procuring entity party; its meaning is already carried by CONTRACT_PROCURED_BY, so a separate role claim would duplicate it.

An opaque publisher party key with no business meaning. ABN is the published identifier where available, and a source-specific party key concept would duplicate identity without adding evidence; it must never be treated as a legal identifier.
An opaque publisher party key with no business meaning; it must never be treated as a legal identifier.

ocid identifies an OCDS contracting process or package that can span multiple releases, awards and contracts, not a single contract or supplier. At this one-release-per-row grain the release id already keys the record and there is no contracting-process entity type.
tender.id repeats the ocid in this snapshot, so it is a process-level key rather than a tender or contract identifier.
A human-readable restatement of procurementMethod ('Limited tender', 'Open tender'); storing both would create a redundant alias of dyn.contract.procurement_method.

In this snapshot title holds short internal reference strings (e.g. NCD11811) that look like agency references rather than descriptive titles; mapping it would create a second identifier concept indistinguishable from dyn.contract.notice_number.
A local join key from contract to award inside the release, not a business fact; the supplier link it supports is already recorded by CONTRACT_AWARDED_TO.
A local award identifier scoped to the release and publisher, not a business identifier and not stable across sources.
Award status uses a separate OCDS codelist and in this snapshot merely repeats contracts[0].status; mapping both would create two competing status claims for one notice until they are reconciled.
In this snapshot the award date equals the release date and the contract dateSigned, so it adds no separate business fact and a third competing date for one notice would be misleading.
A denormalised restatement of parties[].name for the same supplier; mapping both would double-count one name claim.
An internal item identifier local to the release; it is not a business identifier and adds nothing beyond the item classification code already captured.

contactPoint.name mixes organisational unit labels ('FINANCE DIVISION', 'Procurement') with personal names ('Sandra Tuck'). The ontology has no concept for a contact's unit, and personal names must not be stored, so these are dropped rather than mapped.
A contact organisational branch label for the party, not a business fact and not a concept in the current ontology; it is also mixed with agency names rather than branches.
A contact organisational division label for the party, not a business fact and not a concept in the current ontology; it is also mixed with agency names rather than divisions.
A single street-address line (e.g. 'PO Box 3'), often a post-office box. address.full expects a complete formatted address and concatenating lines would invent structure the source does not state.
A single street-address line for a government agency; the same objection as for supplier street addresses applies, and address.full is not a street-line concept.
Not present in the inspected bindings for the procuring entity party; the column profile shows no nonempty values, so no country claim can be made without inventing data.
Not present in the inspected bindings for the procuring entity party; no phone claim can be made without inventing data.
Constant ('contract') schema metadata describing the OCDS release stage, not a business fact; the contract entity already carries that meaning.
Constant ('tender') OCDS schema metadata describing how the process was initiated, with no business fact about the supplier or the contract.
A document language tag ('EN') for the release payload, not a claim about any business or contract.

response.notes: Grain is one release per row; only contracts[0], awards[0] and the role-bound supplier/procuringEntity parties are read, and the bindings must refuse multiple matches rather than selecting one. Contract value is a reported maximum over the contract life, not annual expenditure or business income. UNSPSC item codes describe the contracted goods/services, not the supplier's company-wide industry. ABNs are checksum-validated; no legal form is inferred from party names or ABNs. The procuring entity's country and telephone columns are not present in the inspected bindings and are explicitly unmapped rather than invented. Confidence values are mapping-policy scores, not calibrated probabilities.
